B <= 5.0 (A measured 23.9 on disk). And the arming walks pr/s fall >= 10x, and discards di/s fall >= 10x, B against A. If churn% on B is not below 5.0, the lever is inert here: report it and stop; do not tune.
legs.M2 (cost side, the slow stores): Pages keep their code, so stores to data sharing a code page trap every time. Crimson and Blinx: slow/s on B is REPORTED against A, no threshold on the rise, and cb/s (stores the bitmap answered without a walk) is >= 0.8 of B's slow/s on both titles. FAILS if cb/s < 0.8 * slow/s: then the walks the bitmap exists to remove are still happening. A rise in slow/s above 20x on either title stops the fold until it is priced.
legs.M3 (the number that counts, fps): Crimson, crimson-skies route: B's median gfps >= A's + 2 and >= 26, and B's median G ms < A's. This is a PREDICTION off a BOUND: 23.9% is what the two mechanisms cost, not what removing them returns; the game caps at 30. If M1 holds and M3 fails, the vCPU churn was not what bounded the frame on this route (or the cost moved into M2's slow stores): report both, do not tune.
